title: Synthetic incident rehearsal harness with cost-linked shortflows
creator: Aisha Kwan
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight synthetic-incident rehearsal harness that can execute runbooks-as-tasks in a sandboxed dry-run mode and produce stepwise cost and latency estimates tied to Console telemetry. This enables support engineers and SREs to rehearse remediation playbooks, validate fallbacks, and understand unit economics before touching production.

Scope:
- A CLI + Console UI to load an existing runbook-as-task and run it in 'rehearse' mode against synthetic inputs (fixtures).
- Step-level instrumentation: annotate each action with an estimated token/GPU-second cost, measured latency, and emitted traces that map to Console dashboards.
- What-if cost simulator: combine runtime profiles (from Optimize) with user-configurable batching/quantization knobs to show cost delta for alternate configs.
- RBAC + gating: only users with runbook-rehearse permission can execute; runs create ephemeral sandbox environments with ephemeral credentials.
- Safety: prevent any step that performs destructive actions from running unless a simulated stub is enabled; support both 'noop' stubbing and 'simulated-effect' mode (records expected side effects but does not call external systems).

Implementation notes:
- Reuse runbook-as-task executor (task-api) and add a rehearsal runtime that intercepts external calls.
- Integrate with telemetry SDK to emit per-step metrics: estimated_tokens, gpu_seconds_est, actual_sim_latency_ms, simulated_side_effects (list).
- Cost model: use Optimize's model recommendation profiles and a small local cost estimator to convert gpu_seconds_est -> $ estimate. Persist a snapshot of the estimator with the run metadata.
- Sandbox provisioning: small ephemeral namespace in staging cluster with pre-populated fixtures and a mock external service layer. Runs are isolated and have automatic tear-down.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Synthetic+Rehearsal+Harness (WIP)
- PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-rehearsal/pull/1234
- Demo video (recording of PoC): https://drive.google.com/rehearsal-demo

Rollout plan:
1) PoC + internal demo (engineering + SRE) — Mar 24
2) Feature flag behind `rehearsal-ui` and `rehearsal-cli` — Apr 7
3) Gradual internal onboarding (support, oncall) — Apr 14
4) GA for internal teams — Apr 28 (console-2026.04 release)

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field
acceptance_criteria: CLI can load a runbook-as-task and execute in rehearsal mode with fixtures (no external side effects).
Console shows per-step cost estimate and simulated latency for every rehearsal run.
Telemetry emitted for each step is queryable in the Console (per-run and aggregate).
RBAC prevents unauthorized users from executing rehearsal runs; sandbox namespaces auto-tear-down after 2 hours.
What-if panel computes cost deltas for at least 3 alternate optimizer presets (batching, quantization, model-variant).

implementation_tasks: API: Add /rehearse endpoint to task execution API with dry-run flag
Executor: Implement interceptor layer that swaps network calls with mock adapters
Telemetry: Emit per-step metrics and a rehearsal-run metadata blob to Console
Sandbox: Provision ephemeral staging namespace scripts and quota enforcement
UI: Console panel for starting rehearsals, uploading fixtures, and viewing cost breakdown
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sandboxed runs accidentally call production endpoints. Mitigation: network egress policies and mock adapters by default.
Risk: Cost estimates diverge from actuals. Mitigation: tie estimator to Optimize profiles and provide uncertainty bounds in UI.
Risk: Abuse by users to probe internal services. Mitigation: RBAC + audit logs + run quotas.
